title: Distributed Job Platform — illustrated walkthrough
disclosure: Illustrated, offline walkthrough — not a live execution or benchmark recording.

scenes.title: Accept now. Execute later.
scenes.caption: PostgreSQL owns job state. RabbitMQ carries notifications. The same application can run these roles together or in separate processes.

scenes.title: 202 comes after the commit.
scenes.caption: Job, payload, pending outbox event and saved request outcome commit together. Repeating the same key and input replays the original response.

scenes.title: Confirm delivery intent. Expect duplicates.
scenes.caption: Publish a persistent job reference, require broker confirmation and routing success, then mark the event published. There is no atomic DB/Rabbit commit.

scenes.title: A message is not permission to run.
scenes.caption: Lock the queued job, create a fresh attempt token and lease, increment counters, then commit. Handler execution runs outside that transaction.

scenes.title: Prove ownership again before saving.
scenes.caption: Completion rechecks the current attempt, fresh database time, lease and runtime. Job, completed attempt and result commit atomically.

scenes.title: Save the outcome. Then acknowledge.
scenes.caption: If success commits but the ACK is lost, redelivery sees completed state instead of starting another attempt. ACK can also follow a stored failure or retry schedule.

scenes.title: Two deliveries. One current claim.
scenes.caption: A successful send followed by a failed outbox mark can cause a resend. The second claim sees RUNNING and skips execution; request keys and attempt ownership solve different problems.

scenes.title: One job. Three distinct attempts.
scenes.caption: A simulation configured to fail twice records FAILED, FAILED, COMPLETED. Each due retry creates a new outbox event; four total attempts are allowed per cycle.

scenes.title: A dead worker cannot renew its lease.
scenes.caption: Without renewals, the lease expires. Even before recovery changes RUNNING state, the old attempt no longer has permission to complete or renew.

scenes.title: Record EXPIRED, then use the retry path.
scenes.caption: Recovery locks and rechecks the abandoned attempt. If budget remains, it records EXPIRED and RETRYING; the due retry later creates another notification.

scenes.title: A new token fences the old outcome.
scenes.caption: Replacement attempt A2 completes. Old A1 cannot overwrite its result. These checks protect platform state, not exactly-once external actions or forced cancellation.

scenes.title: Read the tests. Inspect the measurements.
scenes.caption: Real dependency outages, duplicate delivery, killed-worker recovery and local scaling have test/report evidence. No Kubernetes, HA, 1,000 jobs/s or 99.9% availability claim.
